QF.id: VI Public Offering and Corporate Actions_16

question.text: In case of merger/amalgamation involving listed companies, securities under the ISIN of the transferor company are debited and credited to which ISIN?

answer.text: The temporary ISIN of the transferee company (for listed companies)
The existing ISIN of the transferor company
A new permanent ISIN created for the merged entity
The ISIN is not changed during merger

explanation.text: The Logic: For listed companies, securities are debited from the transferor company's ISIN and credited to the temporary ISIN of the transferee company. The securities cannot be transferred until the shares are available for trading. The Trap: A new permanent ISIN may seem logical, but the temporary ISIN with a debit freeze is used first, until trading commences. Note: Clients should be informed that during the transition, the merged shares will sit in a temporary ISIN and cannot be sold until they are listed for trading.
